title: Fluid dynamics of the brane
html:
Fluid dynamics of the brane.

The brane of a quantum observable universe carries a natural fluid dynamics. The substrate parameter q sets the effective brane thickness. At q = 1, the brane is infinitely thin (classical vacuum). At q > 1, it acquires a finite transverse extent governed by the q-deformed contact geometry. The resulting dynamics inherits three features absent from classical Navier--Stokes theory:

  1. Algebraic viscosity. The q-Laplacian \Delta_q (q-Laplacian interpretation) replaces the classical Laplacian, and its eigenvalues are q-integers [k]_q. The viscous dissipation rate is therefore algebraically quantised rather than continuously variable.
  2. Gauge-covariant advection. The \mathrm{SU}(2) connection A defines the velocity field v = \nabla_A S rather than a flat gradient. Advection along v preserves the horizontal self-duality F_A|_H = {*_H}F_A|_H, coupling the fluid motion to the gauge structure.
  3. Topological vortex quantisation. The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) holonomy constrains the circulation around any closed vortex filament \varrho to discrete values [j]_q[j+1]_q, yielding the discrete vortex spectrum.
